functions.name: cudf::distance
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
cudf::size_type cudf::distance(T f, T l)
functions.description: Returns the number of elements between two iterators, equivalent to std::distance but cast to cudf::size_type. Intended for use wherever libcudf APIs expect cudf::size_type indices or sizes. It forwards to std::distance and then static_casts the result.
requirements: f and l must be valid iterators defining a valid range, as required by std::distance.
f and l must be iterators over the same sequence (comparable and compatible), per standard library conventions.
The resulting distance is cast to cudf::size_type; behavior follows static_cast semantics if the true distance does not fit in cudf::size_type (no overflow checking is performed).

functions.name: cudf::operator==
functions.signature: constexpr bool cudf::operator==(cudf::data_type const& lhs, cudf::data_type const& rhs)
functions.description: Compares two cudf::data_type objects for equality. Two data_type values are equal when both their type_id (id()) and fixed-point scale (scale()) are equal. Use to check logical type equivalence within cudf type handling.
requirements: Both arguments must be valid cudf::data_type objects. No additional preconditions are stated.

functions.name: cudf::operator!=
functions.signature: inline bool cudf::operator!=(cudf::data_type const& lhs, cudf::data_type const& rhs)
functions.description: Compares two cudf::data_type objects for inequality. It returns the logical negation of operator==, i.e., true when either the id() or the scale() differ.
requirements: Both arguments must be valid cudf::data_type objects. No additional preconditions are stated.

functions.name: cudf::size_of
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a single element of the specified cudf::data_type. Only fixed-width types are supported. If the type is not fixed-width, the function throws a cudf::logic_error.
requirements: t must denote a fixed-width cudf::data_type; otherwise the function throws cudf::logic_error.
Callers should be prepared to handle an exception for non-fixed-width types (e.g., STRING, LIST, STRUCT).
